title: Ingress and Traffic Routing
description: Route external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to your cluster services using Ingress resources and controllers, with path-based and host-based routing rules.

data.text: An **Ingress** is a Kubernetes API object that manages external access to services, typically HTTP and HTTPS. Instead of exposing every service through its own LoadBalancer — which costs money and creates multiple public endpoints — an Ingress acts as a single entry point that routes traffic to the correct backend service based on rules you define.

An **Ingress controller** is a separate daemon that enforces the Ingress rules. Popular controllers include NGINX Ingress Controller, Traefik, HAProxy, and cloud-managed options like AWS ALB Ingress Controller. Without an installed controller, Ingress resources do nothing.

terms.definition: A Kubernetes API object that exposes HTTP/HTTPS routes from outside the cluster to Services.
A daemon that implements Ingress rules (e.g., NGINX, Traefik).
Routes traffic based on the domain name in the request (e.g., api.example.com vs app.example.com).
Routes traffic based on the URL path (e.g., /api vs /web).
Decrypting HTTPS traffic at the Ingress layer so backend services receive plain HTTP.

data.text: Ingress rules let you direct traffic to different services based on the requested hostname (host-based) or URL path (path-based). This is how a single cluster can serve multiple applications — such as an API at `/api`, a web app at `/`, and a documentation site at `/docs` — from the same external IP.

data.title: Ingress with path and host rules
data.content: Route traffic to different services based on path and hostname.
data.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: app-ingress
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: myapp.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /api
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: api-service
            port:
              number: 8000
      - path: /web
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web-service
            port:
              number: 80

data.text: TLS termination at the Ingress layer means the Ingress controller decrypts incoming HTTPS requests and forwards plain HTTP traffic to the backend services. This centralizes certificate management and reduces the TLS workload on individual application Pods. You store your certificate and private key in a Kubernetes Secret of type `tls`.

data.title: Ingress with TLS termination
data.content: Serve HTTPS traffic using a TLS certificate stored in a Secret.
data.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: secure-ingress
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - secure.myapp.com
    secretName: tls-secret
  rules:
  - host: secure.myapp.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web-service
            port:
              number: 80

data.title: An Ingress resource needs a controller
data.text: Creating an Ingress manifest alone does nothing. You must install an Ingress controller in your cluster first. NGINX Ingress Controller is the most common choice, but Traefik and others are also widely used.
Ingress controllers expose many features through Kubernetes annotations. These are key-value pairs in the Ingress metadata that customize behavior without changing the core Kubernetes API.

data.title: Configure Ingress routing and TLS
data.description: Set up an Ingress controller and define routing rules.
steps: Install the NGINX Ingress Controller in your cluster.
Deploy two services (api-service and web-service) with Pods.
Create an Ingress that routes /api to api-service and / to web-service.
Create a TLS Secret with a self-signed certificate.
Update the Ingress to enable HTTPS with TLS termination.
Verify both HTTP and HTTPS routing with curl.
data.expectedOutcome: External traffic is routed correctly by hostname and path, with HTTPS termination handled by the Ingress.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Ingress provides a single entry point for HTTP/HTTPS traffic, reducing cost and complexity.
An Ingress controller must be installed for Ingress resources to take effect.
Path-based and host-based rules let you serve multiple applications from one IP.
TLS termination at the Ingress layer centralizes certificate management.
Annotations customize Ingress behavior without modifying the Kubernetes API.
data.takeaway: Ingress turns your cluster into a proper web host with flexible, production-grade traffic routing.
